label: related
point: In a footnote the court noted that 42 U.S.C. 10606(b)(4) gives victim-witnesses a right to attend public proceedings unless their testimony would be materially affected; its holding was that any sequestration error was harmless.
change: The Act repealed 10606 and moved crime victims' rights to 18 U.S.C. 3771, with a stronger presence right (exclusion only on clear and convincing evidence that testimony would be materially altered).
why: The repeal touches the victim-presence right the footnote mentioned, but the decision's holding (harmlessness of witnesses' presence at the providence inquiry) does not depend on it.

label: unrelated
point: The court quoted the 'congested airport' definition to describe PHL as congested, as background to a state-law declaratory judgment dispute.
change: The Act updated the referenced FAA benchmark report from 2001 to 2004 or any successor report.
why: A technical update to the report reference has nothing to do with what the decision did with the definition.

label: codifies
point: The court held that the two-year limit in 5121(a) does not cap accrued benefits that rest on a rating or decision existing at the veteran's death, so the widow could recover the full retroactive award.
change: The Act struck 'for a period not to exceed two years' from 5121(a), removing the two-year cap on accrued benefits altogether.
why: The committee report discusses Bonny and Congress went further in the same direction; the new words would decide Bonny's point the same way (full payment), so the law ratifies and extends the result rather than reversing it.

label: related
point: The Court held 18 U.S.C. 48 facially overbroad under the First Amendment, in part because the definition of 'depiction of animal cruelty' in 48(c) reached a vast range of protected depictions.
change: The Act rewrote 48, replacing the broad definitions with a narrower 'animal crush video' offense and turning (c) into an extraterritorial-application clause.
why: Congress responded to Stevens by narrowing the statute to fit the ruling, not by overriding it; the constitutional holding stands, and Stevens's dogfighting videos would still fall outside the new crush-video offense.

label: unrelated
point: The court cited 1400(d)(1)(A) for the general proposition that each child with a disability is entitled to a FAPE, then applied the Rowley standard and upheld the school's IEP.
change: The Act added 'further education' to the purpose of preparing children and changed 'systemic-change activities' to 'system improvement activities.'
why: Cited only as a general purposes statement; the wording change did not bear on the decision's application of the Rowley standard to the methodology dispute.

label: override_express
point: The Court held that 1252(a)(1) and (a)(2)(C) speak only of 'judicial review' and do not clearly strip district courts of habeas jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. 2241 over criminal aliens' removal challenges.
change: The REAL ID Act inserted 'including section 2241 of title 28, or any other habeas corpus provision' into the jurisdiction-stripping provisions of 1252(a)(2) and added a petition for review as the exclusive means of review.
why: The new words supply exactly the clear statement St. Cyr found missing, eliminating 2241 habeas review, and the committee report names St. Cyr as the decision being answered.

label: related
point: The court relied on 5401's statement of purposes (reducing injuries, deaths, insurance costs and property damage) to hold that HUD could and had to weigh general safety and damage costs, not only consumer price increases, in upholding the post-Hurricane Andrew wind standards.
change: The Act rewrote 5401 into findings and purposes that emphasize affordability and homeownership, while keeping protection against injuries, insurance costs and property damage 'consistent with the other purposes.'
why: The report passage names the case in arguing about the rewrite, but the new purposes still include reducing injury and property damage, so HUD's duty to weigh them, and the decision's result, would likely survive.

label: override_express
point: Applying Bailey's 'active employment' reading of 'uses' in 924(c)(1) retroactively, the court vacated a conviction where the gun merely sat in a handbag with cocaine.
change: The Act restructured 924(c)(1) to also punish anyone who 'in furtherance of any such crime, possesses a firearm,' with graded minimums.
why: The committee report cites this decision among post-Bailey vacaturs it meant to address, and under the new possession-in-furtherance prong, a gun stored with drugs, as in Turner, can support a conviction.

label: codifies
point: The court affirmed the asylum denial, finding no well-founded fear and that robbery was not shown to be aimed at the petitioner on account of his political opinion.
change: The REAL ID Act added a burden-of-proof clause requiring that a protected ground be 'at least one central reason' for persecution, plus corroboration and credibility rules.
why: The committee report cites Useinovic approvingly as an example of the nexus analysis the new 'one central reason' standard adopts; the decision would come out the same way under the new words.

label: override_express
point: The Court held that 10 U.S.C. 821 (Art. 21) conditions the use of military commissions on compliance with the law of war, including Common Article 3, so the Guantanamo commission lacked power to proceed (and a plurality found conspiracy not triable by commission).
change: The Military Commissions Act added that 821 does not apply to military commissions established under new chapter 47A.
why: By making 821 inapplicable to the new commissions, Congress removed the statutory basis of Hamdan's holding, and the legislative record names Hamdan as what the Act responds to.

label: codifies
point: The court affirmed a $64 million FCA judgment (treble damages plus per-claim penalties under 3729(a)), rejecting an Excessive Fines challenge; elsewhere the opinion applied a natural-tendency materiality test.
change: FERA restructured 3729(a), replaced 'to get a false or fraudulent claim paid or approved' with 'material to a false or fraudulent claim,' and broadened conspiracy and reverse-false-claims liability.
why: The committee report cites Rogan approvingly for the materiality definition Congress wrote in; the damages and penalty rule the decision applied is unchanged.

label: related
point: The district court denied cross-motions for summary judgment, finding a fact issue over whether the taxpayers' pipelines were 7-year gathering systems (Class 13.2) or 15-year trunk lines (Class 46.0), and declining to follow Duke Energy.
change: The Act amended 168(e) (the shown changes add qualified leasehold-improvement and restaurant property; the Act also made natural gas gathering lines 7-year property prospectively).
why: The report cites this decision as part of the circuit conflict, but the prospective gathering-line rule does not reverse the court's fact-bound ruling, and the shown changes to the cited words are on other property.

label: unrelated
point: The court cited 2113(b) as the bank-theft offense of conviction, which the guidelines index to larceny rather than burglary, and reversed a burglary-guideline sentence.
change: The Act replaced the misdemeanor fine cap of 'not more than $1,000' with 'fined under this title.'
why: A change in the fine for the under-$1,000 offense has nothing to do with the guideline-selection holding.

label: unrelated
point: The court held that an alter ego claim against the parent was not estate property, so the 362(a)(3) automatic stay did not bar the creditor's state-court action.
change: BAPCPA narrowed 362(a)(8)'s Tax Court stay to particular corporate and individual tax liabilities.
why: The change is to a different paragraph (Tax Court proceedings) and does not affect 362(a)(3).

label: unrelated
point: The court cited the ADA (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.) only through an FMLA regulation defining inability to perform job functions.
change: The ADAAA rewrote the ADA findings in 12101, rejecting narrow readings of 'disability.'
why: The decision did not rely on the ADA findings; the cite is in passing.

label: unrelated
point: The court noted that the Motor Carrier Act defines 'person' to include a trustee or receiver, which it found inconclusive on whether a debtor in possession could recover undercharges.
change: SAFETEA-LU renumbered the 13102 definitions, so paragraph (16) became 'motor vehicle'; the 'person' definition moved.
why: Renumbering only.

label: unrelated
point: The court cited the IDEA generally (20 U.S.C. 1401 et seq.) in a dispute over a child's placement in the least restrictive environment.
change: The IDEIA rewrote many definitions in 1401 (e.g., an exclusion for surgically implanted devices).
why: The section was cited only as the start of the Act; no definition was at issue.

label: unrelated
point: The court cited 62(a) to note that adjusted gross income already reflects certain above-the-line deductions, which risked double-counting payroll deductions in an undue-hardship analysis.
change: The Act extended the teacher-expense deduction years in 62(a)(2)(D) to 2012 and 2013.
why: Extending a year list for an unrelated deduction does not touch the decision's point.

label: unrelated
point: The court affirmed denial of a 3582(c)(2) sentence reduction because the defendant's guideline range was not lowered by the crack amendment given a supplemental drug-quantity finding.
change: The First Step Act let defendants move for compassionate release under 3582(c)(1)(A) after exhausting BOP remedies.
why: The change is to (c)(1)(A), not the (c)(2) guideline-amendment eligibility rule the decision applied.

label: unrelated
point: The court cited 1400(d) for the IDEA's general purposes before deciding an attorneys'-fees question under 1415(i)(3).
change: The IDEIA added 'further education' and changed 'systemic-change' to 'system improvement' in the purposes.
why: The purposes wording has nothing to do with the fee question decided.

label: related
point: The court held that VA had to give claimant-specific 5103(a) notice of what was needed to prove veteran status (some tailoring for Philippine claimants), but affirmed because the Board's finding of compliance was not clearly erroneous.
change: The Act directed the Secretary to issue regulations specifying notice contents by type of claim, including the general information and evidence needed for each claim's basic elements.
why: The report names Palor as an example of increasingly case-specific notice rules, but the new words still require notice on basic elements such as veteran status and do not clearly reverse Palor's rule or its result.

label: unrelated
point: On cross-motions for partial summary judgment the court held the City's leave and overtime policies violated USERRA, citing 4323 only for jurisdiction.
change: The Act added referral deadlines, made equity powers mandatory where appropriate, and moved the no-state-limitations clause out of 4323(i) (into a new no-limitations rule in 4327).
why: The report cites a later 2003 ruling in the same case on the statute of limitations; this decision used 4323 only for jurisdiction, which is unchanged.
